item.description:
Crema 1.4.0

  • The documents said what the app used to do
  • A label that scopes itself needs no paragraph excusing it
  • The Dock was scaffolding for a diagnosis that turned out wrong
  • The card was drawn on hardware the author does not own
  • The screen had a top and no bottom, so nothing had a place
  • A test that asserted an order nothing promises
  • The tiles were three grey rectangles with a smudge on them
  • The menu gets the switch it was only ever talking about
  • Two lines that sent the reader somewhere, and one that blamed macOS
  • The rule the permissions tab was following in words but not in symbols
  • The card looked welded to the bezel because it was painted like one
  • A binding read by nothing, left where a comparison used to be
  • The five joins in the composition root that could go wrong in silence
  • A function carrying two doc comments, the first refuting the second
  • Two documents describing an integration that shipped weeks ago
  • The three availability guards that could stall had nothing holding them
  • A drag nothing honoured now comes back instead of standing there
  • The bar the drag left behind was the one being echoed back
  • The retry button did nothing in the window it was written for
  • The one write that landed after an await without asking whose world it was
  • Two test helpers that could hide the failure they exist to show
  • A failing test that kills the process is not a failing test
  • Eleven sentences that outlived the design they described
  • A copy of the app icon that nothing pointed at
  • Four documents that had drifted, and the release gate that was missing one
  • A swallowed key on a channel with no control now goes back to the system
  • Settings finally mentions the neighbour it has been working with
  • Three documents that had stopped describing this app, and a pin declared impossible
  • The mirror guard is real; the reason written beside it was not
  • The keyboard backlight can arrive after launch, and now it is allowed to
  • A HUD names a role, not a display it may not have
  • The no-emoji rule says which strings it is about
  • The catalog rule finally has something enforcing it
  • Pick the style by looking at it
  • Six claims of mine, checked against the sources instead of my memory
  • Docs catch up with the key that follows the pointer
  • The brightness key now acts on the screen you are looking at
  • I asked through the wrong door and called the answer a limitation
  • Permissions names the one the app needed and never mentioned
  • Give the Settings tabs their own files before two more rows go in
  • The menu says what Crema is doing, not only when something breaks
  • The bar drew on every screen because I threw away which one was named
  • The neighbour's brightness can be written but not read
  • Sample a clock that cannot lie, and say the fallback out loud
  • The last five, and the critics earned their keep
  • Holding a key through a suspension no longer mutes the rest of the hold
  • Research says one of my findings was wrong, and corroborates another
  • Two seams that were never reachable, and I was wrong about one of them
  • Seven comments that described a machine we no longer run
  • Nothing gates the release script, and the update panel opens blank
  • Five smaller edges, and a claim that was backwards
  • Three promises the code had stopped keeping
  • Sampling volume no longer freezes the app it is drawing for
  • Brightness addressed the menu bar's display, not the built-in one
  • Xcode's own Archive built an app that could not open
  • The write-health axis only counts what it claims to count
  • An async signature is not a suspension point
  • A live stream is not 292 thousand years long
  • Seventeen: the onboarding's order, and a guard that needed two displays
  • Two more, and a lesson about what a value can witness
  • Three more witnesses, one of them for a test that raced itself
  • Give the expensive invariants a witness
  • Scope the HUD where it is DRAWN, not only where it is touchable
  • A HUD belongs to the display it names
  • Send the drag back to whoever drew the bar
  • Say when the neighbour is feeding us, and stop drawing over it
  • Let BetterDisplay keep the keys, and draw the HUD from what it says
  • When another app takes the media keys first, name it
  • Sample the clock instead of counting ticks: the bar stops falling behind
  • CLAUDE.md: the launch-at-login preference is an intent, not a state
  • Notice when macOS revokes launch-at-login, and say so
  • A real download button, drawn instead of borrowed
  • Showcase with real album art: the three styles, captured live
  • README: a big Download-for-macOS button under the hero
  • chore(release): appcast 1.2.0 — the feed goes live, docs flip to the shipped truth
